## Buffered Channel

Berbeda dengan unbuffered channel, **buffered channel** memiliki kapasitas internal. Send hanya memblokir ketika buffer **penuh**, dan receive hanya memblokir ketika buffer **kosong**.

## Membuat Buffered Channel

```go
ch := make(chan int, 3) // buffer berkapasitas 3
```

## Perilaku Non-Blocking

```go
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	ch := make(chan string, 2)

	// Ini TIDAK memblokir karena buffer masih ada tempat
	ch <- "ping"
	ch <- "pong"

	// Buffer penuh — send berikutnya akan memblokir!
	// ch <- "overflow" // ini akan deadlock jika tidak ada goroutine lain

	fmt.Println(<-ch) // ping
	fmt.Println(<-ch) // pong
}
```

## Pattern: Semaphore dengan Buffered Channel

Buffered channel sering digunakan sebagai semaphore untuk membatasi concurrency:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	// Batasi maksimal 3 goroutine berjalan bersamaan
	sem := make(chan struct{}, 3)

	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		i := i
		sem <- struct{}{} // acquire slot
		go func() {
			defer func() { <-sem }() // release slot
			fmt.Printf("worker %d running\n", i)
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
		}()
	}

	// Tunggu semua selesai
	for i := 0; i < cap(sem); i++ {
		sem <- struct{}{}
	}
}
```

## len dan cap pada Channel

```go
ch := make(chan int, 5)
ch <- 1
ch <- 2
ch <- 3

fmt.Println(len(ch)) // 3 — jumlah elemen saat ini
fmt.Println(cap(ch)) // 5 — kapasitas total buffer
```

## Kapan Gunakan Buffered?

| Situasi | Pilihan |
|---|---|
| Sinkronisasi ketat (rendezvous) | Unbuffered |
| Decoupling producer-consumer | Buffered |
| Rate limiting / semaphore | Buffered |
| Batch processing | Buffered |

## Buffered Channel

Unlike unbuffered channels, a **buffered channel** has internal capacity. Send only blocks when the buffer is **full**, and receive only blocks when the buffer is **empty**.

## Creating a Buffered Channel

```go
ch := make(chan int, 3) // buffer with capacity 3
```

## Non-Blocking Behavior

```go
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	ch := make(chan string, 2)

	// These do NOT block because buffer has space
	ch <- "ping"
	ch <- "pong"

	// Buffer is full — the next send would block!
	// ch <- "overflow" // would deadlock without another goroutine

	fmt.Println(<-ch) // ping
	fmt.Println(<-ch) // pong
}
```

## Pattern: Semaphore with Buffered Channel

Buffered channels are often used as semaphores to limit concurrency:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	// Limit to max 3 goroutines running simultaneously
	sem := make(chan struct{}, 3)

	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		i := i
		sem <- struct{}{} // acquire slot
		go func() {
			defer func() { <-sem }() // release slot
			fmt.Printf("worker %d running\n", i)
			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
		}()
	}

	// Wait for all to finish
	for i := 0; i < cap(sem); i++ {
		sem <- struct{}{}
	}
}
```

## len and cap on Channels

```go
ch := make(chan int, 5)
ch <- 1
ch <- 2
ch <- 3

fmt.Println(len(ch)) // 3 — current number of elements
fmt.Println(cap(ch)) // 5 — total buffer capacity
```

## When to Use Buffered?

| Situation | Choice |
|---|---|
| Strict synchronization (rendezvous) | Unbuffered |
| Decoupling producer-consumer | Buffered |
| Rate limiting / semaphore | Buffered |
| Batch processing | Buffered |
